study type: Cross-sectional survey with retrospective data collection
exposure: receiving a pacifier in the hospital
staff helping mothers learn how to breastfeed in the hospital
starting and feeding only breast milk in the hospital
receiving a phone number to call for help with breastfeeding from the hospital
cohort: A stratified systematic sample of 5,770 mothers participating in the Utah Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) between 2012 and 2015 were included.
finding: Mothers who reported receiving a pacifier, receiving formula, or having staff help them learn how to breastfeed in the hospital had a higher prevalence of terminating breastfeeding before 2 months, while exclusively breastfeeding in the hospital and receiving a helpline number were associated with a lower prevalence.
